ADDED i1: Tests that {@link LookupTranslator} correctly handles supplementary (non-BMP) Unicode code points as lookup keys. Supplementary characters are represented as tw
ADDED i2: U+1D54F MATHEMATICAL DOUBLE-STRUCK CAPITAL X — a supplementary code point (outside the Basic Multilingual Plane) that Java encodes as a two-{@code char} surroga
ADDED i3: A supplementary key must count as exactly one Unicode code point when consumed, even though it occupies two {@code char} slots in the underlying Java string.
ADDED i5: Create a translator that maps the supplementary key to the ASCII letter "X".
ADDED i6: --- Verify that the key translates correctly ---
ADDED i7: The translator must report consumption in code points, not in Java chars: the two-char surrogate pair is a single code point, so the return value must be 1.
ADDED i8: The translator must write the mapped replacement value.
